title: Enhancement of Tensile Properties of Cast Beta-Type Titanium Alloy by Aging Treatment
abstract: Aging treatment of as-cast beta titanium alloy Ti-15Mo-5Zr at 520C for 4 h precipitated fine alpha phase within the beta matrix. Ultimate tensile strength increased from 712 MPa (as-cast) to 895 MPa while elongation dropped from 18.2% to 12.4%. The strengthening was attributed to Orowan bypass of coherent precipitates.

title: Microstructural Evolution and Mechanical Properties of a Near-Beta Titanium Alloy During Solution plus Aging Heat Treatments
abstract: Near-beta titanium alloy Ti-5Al-5Mo-5V-3Cr (Ti-5553) was solution treated at 820C and aged between 500 and 600C. Increasing aging temperature coarsened alpha laths from 45 nm to 120 nm and reduced tensile strength from 1420 MPa to 1265 MPa while fracture toughness increased from 45 to 62 MPa·m^0.5. A strength-toughness trade-off window is identified at 550C.

title: Effect of Aging Temperature on Alpha Precipitation Kinetics in Ti-6Al-4V
abstract: Isothermal aging of Ti-6Al-4V between 510 and 540C showed alpha phase grain coarsening from 60 nm to 140 nm following the LSW coarsening law. Tensile strength decreased from 1365 MPa to 1240 MPa and elongation increased from 6.5% to 10.5%. The Hall-Petch relationship described the strength-grain size dependence with k = 0.42 MPa·m^0.5.

title: Tensile Behavior of TC18 Titanium Alloy Under Multiple Aging Schedules
abstract: TC18 (Ti-4.5Al-5Mo-5V-6Cr-1Nb) was aged at 450 to 550C for 4 h. Yield strength ranged 1238 to 1381 MPa and ultimate tensile strength 1363 to 1516 MPa with elongation 9.0 to 10.3%. The best strength-ductility balance occurred at 500C. Overaging above 550C coarsened grain boundary alpha and reduced strength.

title: Multistage Aging of Ti-6Al-7Nb for Orthopedic Implants: Mechanical and Corrosion Perspectives
abstract: Solution treated Ti-6Al-7Nb underwent single and duplex aging. Duplex aging (500C/8h + 600C/2h) yielded yield strength 871 MPa, ultimate tensile strength 940 MPa, elongation 11.5%, and a 34% reduction in wear rate versus the single-aged condition. Passive film stability was confirmed by potentiodynamic polarization in simulated body fluid.

title: Precipitation Strengthening Mechanisms in Metastable Beta Titanium Alloys: A Review
abstract: Review of omega-phase assisted alpha nucleation, isothermal omega metastability, and alpha2 ordering in metastable beta titanium alloys. Discusses Orowan versus shearing transition as precipitate size exceeds 6 nm, and maps alloy composition windows for precipitation hardening response.

title: Hot Deformation and Subsequent Aging of TC4 Titanium Alloy Produced by Additive Manufacturing
abstract: Laser powder bed fused Ti-6Al-4V was hot isostatically pressed (920C/120MPa/2h) and subsequently aged at 550C/4h. Post-aging ultimate tensile strength reached 1088 MPa with elongation 8.9%, exceeding the wrought annealed minimum. Columnar prior-beta grain structure persisted through the thermal cycle.

title: Alpha-Case Formation and Its Deleterious Effect on Fatigue of Aged Titanium Alloys
abstract: Alpha-case layer of 40 to 120 micrometers formed during air aging at 600 to 700C reduced high-cycle fatigue life of Ti-6Al-4V by up to 45%. Vacuum or argon aging eliminated alpha-case. Fatigue strength at 10^7 cycles recovered to 512 MPa after machined removal of the layer.

title: Phase Field Simulation of Alpha Precipitate Growth in Beta Titanium: Parameter Identification Against Aging Experiments
abstract: Phase field simulations of alpha precipitation in Ti-5553 were calibrated against dilatometry and hardness data from isothermal aging at 500 to 600C. The identified interfacial energy of 0.19 J/m^2 and diffusivity pre-exponential reproduced experimental mean lath thickness within 8% error over 10 hours.

title: Cryogenic Tensile Properties of Aged Beta Titanium Alloys for Deep-Sea Applications
abstract: Aged Ti-15Mo-5Zr and Ti-5553 were tested at 77K, 200K and 298K. Ultimate tensile strength of aged Ti-5553 increased from 1350 MPa at 298K to 1610 MPa at 77K while elongation decreased from 9.8% to 4.1%. Adiabatic heating during deformation was observed above 1200 MPa flow stress.

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Aging Parameters in Alpha-Beta Titanium Alloys
abstract: Gradient boosted trees trained on 412 published aging datasets predicted ultimate tensile strength within mean absolute error of 42 MPa and optimal aging temperature within 22C. Mo equivalent and aging temperature dominated feature importance. The model is released with an interactive parameter explorer.

title: Hydrogen Embrittlement Susceptibility of Aged Versus Solution Treated Ti-6Al-4V
abstract: Cathodically charged specimens showed that the aged condition (550C/4h) was 2.3 times more susceptible to hydrogen embrittlement than the solution treated condition, attributed to hydride precipitation at alpha-beta interfaces. Fracture toughness dropped 31% at 1000 wppm hydrogen.

title: In-Situ Synchrotron Observation of Alpha Precipitation During In-Situ Aging of Ti-5553
abstract: In-situ synchrotron SAXS during aging at 550C revealed three-stage alpha precipitation: nucleation burst (0 to 15 min), growth (15 to 120 min), and coarsening (>120 min). Volume fraction saturated at 0.34. Nucleation rate peaked at 2.1e21 m^-3 s^-1 during stage one.

title: Superplastic Forming of Fine-Grained Aged Titanium Sheet After Severe Plastic Deformation
abstract: Equal channel angular pressed and subsequently aged Ti-6Al-4V sheet exhibited superplastic elongation of 480% at 850C with strain rate sensitivity m = 0.53. Equiaxed fine grains of 2.1 micrometers were retained after aging due to pinning by precipitates.

title: Comparative Oxidation Kinetics of Aged Titanium Alloys in Air up to 700C
abstract: Parabolic oxidation rate constants of aged Ti-6Al-4V, Ti-5553 and commercially pure titanium were measured between 500 and 700C. Activation energies ranged from 214 to 258 kJ/mol. Oxide scale was predominantly rutile TiO2 with minor Al2O3 in alpha lamellae regions.

title: Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing of TC18: Effect of Interpass Temperature on Post-Aging Properties
abstract: Wire arc additive manufactured TC18 with interpass temperatures of 150 and 450C were solution treated and aged at 500C/4h. The 150C interpass condition showed 12% higher tensile strength after aging due to finer prior-beta colonies. Anisotropy was reduced from 8.2% to 3.5% by post-aging cold rolling.

title: Low-Cycle Fatigue Behavior of Duplex Aged Ti-5553: Mean Stress Effects and Life Modeling
venue: Fatigue & Fracture of Engineering Materials & Structures
abstract: Duplex aged Ti-5553 (870C/1h + 550C/8h) showed mean-stress-corrected low-cycle fatigue life described by a Smith-Watson-Topper parameter with fitted coefficient 921 and exponent -0.71. Cyclic softening of 14% occurred within the first 50 reversals at total strain amplitude 1.2%.

title: Grain Boundary Alpha Engineering in Beta-Processed TC4: Balancing Dwell Fatigue and Fracture Toughness
abstract: Continuous grain boundary alpha networks in beta-processed Ti-6Al-4V were interrupted by controlled pre-aging at 600C for 30 min before final aging at 550C. Dwell fatigue strength at 10^7 cycles improved 22% while fracture toughness decreased only 6%, achieving a combined property window not reported previously.
